defects: Hypothesis `nontrivial_F : Nontrivial F` asserts the field itself is nontrivial (0 ≠ 1), not that each absolute value v i is nontrivial (IsNontrivial); the actual required hypothesis that each v i is a nontrivial absolute value is missing entirely.

Hypothesis `v i ≠ v j` (function inequality) is used instead of pairwise inequivalence (¬ IsEquiv); two absolute values can be distinct as functions yet equivalent (e.g. v and v^t), so this hypothesis is strictly weaker than required and does not capture the mathematical content needed for the theorem.

The conclusion's topology on `ι → F` comes from an arbitrary, unconstrained `[TopologicalSpace (ι → F)]` instance instead of the product of the topologies induced by each v i (via WithAbs); this completely disconnects the density conclusion from the absolute values v, making the statement either underspecified or a different/false claim depending on the chosen instance.
Uses `[Fintype ι]` instead of `[Finite ι]`, an unnecessary strengthening (requires a Fintype instance/data rather than the Prop-valued Finite).
